instruction: Skip ahead 10 seconds in the video to see what follows.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires skipping forward 10 seconds in VLC video. Video starts at 15 seconds (--start-time=15), so after skipping +10s it should be at minimum 25 seconds. Agent must use right arrow key, Ctrl+Right, or seek bar. Evaluator checks VLC HTTP status to verify <time> element is >= 25 seconds. Verified that VLC status.xml contains time element showing current playback position in seconds.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts VLC playback time via HTTP interface status.xml, which is the standard method to query VLC state
Metric correctly compares actual playback time against minimum threshold (>= 25 seconds)
Expected value is semantically correct: min_time=25 represents initial 15 seconds + 10 second skip
Evaluator provides complete coverage of the instruction requirement (verify 10-second forward skip)
Parameter handling is correct: metric directly accesses expected.get('min_time') when type='rule', which matches framework behavior
Edge cases handled gracefully: HTTP errors return None, XML parsing errors return 0.0, missing time element defaults to 0
No postconfig needed as VLC HTTP interface remains accessible during evaluation
